summary: 职业歌手的声带须频繁承受摩擦，密集演出等因素会提高损伤风险。声乐教练和外科医生对训练方式与手术的作用有不同看法，文章借此讨论歌手如何维持职业生涯。
logic: 声乐教学和手术的分歧

paragraphs.brief: 声带振动怎样产生歌声
sentences: Singing is a tough business.
唱歌是件费力的事。
Every vocal performance involves hundreds of thousands of micro-collisions of a thin pair of muscular strips called the vocal cords, located in the larynx in the throat.
演唱一次，喉内那一对叫声带的薄肌带就会产生数十万次微小碰撞。
When we are breathing in, they remain apart; when we sing or speak, air is pushed up out of the lungs, and the edges of the cords come together in a rapid chopping motion.
吸气时双侧声带分开，说话或唱歌时气流从肺部向上推出，声带边缘快速开合。
The air causes the cords to vibrate, creating sound.
气流带动声带振动，从而发出声音。
The greater the vibration, the higher the pitch, and when a soprano hits the highest notes her vocal cords are vibrating 1,000 times per second.
声带振动越快，音调越高，女高音唱到最高音时声带每秒可振动一千次。
This transforms a burst of air from her lungs into a sound powerful enough to shatter glass.
肺中呼出的一股气，便能化成强烈到足以震碎玻璃的声音。
paragraphs.gist: 歌唱时肺部气流使声带快速接触、振动而发声，女高音唱最高音时每秒可振动约一千次，可见声带承受的运动量之大。

paragraphs.brief: 过度用嗓和早期损伤信号
sentences: Beautiful singing requires flexible cords, but the friction caused by prolonged overuse can erode their fine, spongy surface and lead to tiny bruises.
优美歌唱需要柔韧的声带，但长期过度使用造成的摩擦会损伤精细、海绵状的表面，并导致微小淤伤。
Eventually, nodules, polyps or cysts form on the vocal folds, distorting the sound they create.
声带上最终可能长出结节、息肉或囊肿，令声音失真。
For a singer, the first sign of trouble is often the ‘wobble’: the voice fluctuates on and off key because the damaged cords have lost the ability to resonate properly.
歌手最早察觉的常是声音发颤、音准忽高忽低，因为受损声带已不能正常共鸣。
Often, there is a ‘hole’, a point on the musical scale where a singer’s vibrating vocal cords fail to produce the proper tone.
音阶上常会出现一个“空洞”，即歌手声带虽在振动，却发不出正确音调。
The sound produced will be flat, or worse still, barely audible.
这时声音会偏低，严重时甚至几乎听不见。
It was once unheard of for a singer to perform with a faulty voice.
过去歌手嗓子有问题还上台演出是闻所未闻的。
However, in recent times, it has become more common for performances to be interrupted, or even cancelled due to the inability of the performer to continue.
近来因表演者唱不下去而中断甚至取消演出的情况却越来越常见。
Some opera singers complain of year-round cold symptoms, and steroid injections and numerous other drugs are often used to get a struggling singer through a performance.
有些歌剧演员抱怨常年像患了感冒，时常得靠注射类固醇或其他药物撑过一场演出。
But continuing to sing can cause more damage and create voice-ruining scars, similar to when a football player continues to play with a damaged knee and eventually needs surgery.
但继续唱可能加重损伤，留下毁坏嗓音的瘢痕，就像球员膝伤后继续踢球，最终不得不开刀一样。
paragraphs.gist: 长期摩擦会损伤声带并形成结节等病变，歌手可能出现音准不稳甚至某个音发不出来，带伤坚持演出还可能留下瘢痕。

paragraphs.brief: 职业环境增加声带受伤风险
sentences: There is no precise data on the number of performers who have undergone surgical procedures, but it is estimated that thousands have been under the knife.
没有确切统计显示多少表演者做过手术，但估计已有数千人接受过治疗。
Dusty theatres, stuffy airplane cabins, erratic eating and sleeping patterns and stress all affect the vocal cords.
积尘的剧院、通风不畅的机舱、饮食睡眠不定时和压力都会影响声带。

Add to all this the occupational hazard – at least in opera and classical music – of taking on roles that require artists to sing beyond their natural range, and a singer’s cords become extremely susceptible to injury.
此外，至少在歌剧和古典音乐中，演员还可能接下须唱出天然音域之外的角色，种种因素使声带极易受伤。
paragraphs.gist: 剧院灰尘、闷热机舱、作息不规律和压力都会影响声带，歌剧演员若再承担超出自然音域的角色，受伤的机会就更高。

paragraphs.brief: 损伤年轻化与崇尚音量
sentences: Will Crutchfield, a conductor and vocal coach, laments the fact that this vocal burnout is cutting short careers and diminishing the power of opera, and he feels that audiences have become accustomed to hearing voices which are not in peak condition.
指挥兼声乐教练威尔·克拉奇菲尔德惋惜，用嗓过度正缩短歌手的职业生涯、削弱歌剧的表现力，观众也已经习惯了状态并不理想的声音。

When he first highlighted the problem, he noticed that it didn’t affect singers until they were in their 30s, but now even singers in their 20s are undergoing medical procedures to save their careers.
他最初指出这问题时，歌手往往到三十多岁才受影响，如今甚至有二十多岁的歌手为了保住事业而接受治疗。
These injuries have been linked to a shift in what we consider quality singing.
这些损伤与人们判断优质演唱的标准发生改变有关。
Across all genres, it has become normal to believe that louder is better, and singers are pushing their vocal cords like never before.
各个流派都逐渐流行“越响越好”的观念，歌手正以前所未有的强度使用声带。
New waves of medical research into dysphonia, or the inability to properly produce sound, bear this out.
关于发声障碍，即无法正常发出声音的新一批医学研究，也印证了这一点。
In the Western world, vocal abuse is surprisingly common in all professions that rely on the voice, from schoolteachers to opera singers.
在西方世界，从教师到歌剧演员，各种依靠声音工作的职业中过度用嗓都出奇地普遍。
paragraphs.gist: 指挥克拉奇菲尔德发现，接受声带治疗的歌手越来越年轻，崇尚音量的演唱风气也与教师等用嗓职业普遍出现的过度用声相呼应。

paragraphs.brief: 手术与改进演唱教育之争
sentences: Steven Zeitels, a specialist vocal cord surgeon, believes that pioneering surgery is the way forward.
声带外科专家史蒂文·泽特尔斯认为，创新手术是值得发展的方向。
He is working on a futuristic solution which will involve implanting a gel made of biomaterial in the tissue of damaged vocal cords to restore pliability, and therefore the voice.
他正在研究把生物材料凝胶植入受损声带组织，以恢复声带的柔韧性，进而恢复嗓音。
However, some research studies argue that surgery is not necessarily a lasting fix.
然而，一些研究认为，手术不一定是一个持久的解决办法。
According to Lisa Paglin, a singer turned voice coach, Zeitels has simply found a temporary remedy.
由歌手转任声乐教练的莉萨·帕格林则认为，泽特尔斯找到的只是权宜之计。
‘Unless a singer makes major changes, “return to performing” means a return to the vocal abuse that put him/her on the operating table in the first place’.
她说，除非歌手作出重大改变，否则重回舞台就是回到当初让自己上手术台的不当用嗓方式。
Her coaching partner Marianna Brilla agrees.
她的教学搭档玛丽安娜·布里拉也持相同意见。
‘You cannot solve the problem by simply relieving the symptom.’
她说，仅仅缓解症状无法解决问题本身。

One observation Paglin and Brilla have made from working with older, classically trained singers is the way that they use the natural up-down release of the diaphragm to produce sound, rather than relying on their vocal cords.
两人与受过古典训练的年长歌手合作时发现，他们利用横膈膜自然的上下起伏发声，不把负担全压在声带上。
For Brilla, this represents a real discovery: the root of the problem today is in classrooms.
对布瑞拉来说，这是一个真正的发现：今天问题的根源在于教室。
She believes that students are graduating from music academies without having learned this natural singing method.
她认为，学生从音乐学院毕业时，没有学习这种自然的唱歌方法。
In her opinion, today’s students ‘don’t know how to sing, and it’s leading to injury’.
在她看来，今天的学生"不知道怎么唱歌，它导致伤害。"
paragraphs.gist: 外科医生尝试用凝胶恢复声带弹性，两位声乐教练则认为，若学校不教学生运用横膈膜、歌手不改变用声习惯，手术效果难以持久。

paragraphs.brief: 长期演唱磨损与手术选择
sentences: Is it possible that teaching people to sing differently could cure damaged vocal cords forever?
教歌手改用另一种唱法，能让受损声带彻底康复吗？
Zeitels is dismissive of such an approach, and quick to deny that his clients’ vocal problems are caused by bad technique.
Zeitels对这种做法持否定态度，并很快否认他的客户的发声问题是由坏技术造成的。
‘People used to think if you needed an operation it meant you don’t know how to sing.
人们常想如果你需要手术意味着你不会唱歌
The people I see – they know how to sing!’
我所见的人，他们知道怎么唱。
Zeitels believes that medical specialists are becoming increasingly important to the arts, given that any athletic endeavour will eventually take a toll if done for long enough.
泽特尔斯认为医学专家在艺术界正变得越来越重要，因为任何身体活动只要做得足够久，最终都会造成损耗。
Robert Sataloff, who has performed voice-corrective surgery on several award-winning performers, also resents the notion that surgery is not a sensible way to keep singers healthy.
曾为多位获奖演员做过嗓音矫治手术的罗伯特·萨塔洛夫，也不赞成否定手术在维持歌手健康方面的价值。
He believes that surgery, combined with proper education on the dangers of improper singing technique, can keep people on stage for longer.
他相信手术加上适当的教育来了解不当唱歌技巧的危险性能使人们在舞台上呆得更久
He concedes that surgery is not a perfect solution, and it probably never will be, but it is an option.
他承认手术并不是一个完美的解决方案，可能永远不会，但这是一个选项。
paragraphs.gist: 两位医生指出，即使技巧娴熟，长期表演也会损耗嗓音，手术若配合正确的用声教育，仍可能帮助歌手延长舞台生涯。

items.en: examples of some of the environmental factors which affect singers
items.zh: 影响歌手的一些环境因素的例子
items.why: 题干中的 environmental factors 指的是外部环境条件。C 段这一句直接列举了剧院、飞机机舱、饮食睡眠模式和压力等外在环境 / 生活条件对声带的影响，是“例子 (examples) ”的罗列，因此选 C。其他段要么讲解生理机制 (A)、要么讲初期症状 (B)、手术与观念 (D-F),都不是在集中举环境例子。

items.en: a reference to a lack of awareness of a correct singing technique
items.zh: 提及对正确唱歌技巧缺乏认识
items.why: 题干说的是“缺乏对正确唱歌技巧的认识”。 Paglin & Brilla 指出现代学生没学到正确方法，直接说 don't know how to sing,说明对正确技巧缺乏认知，因此选 E。其他段虽然提到技术 (如 F 段说并不是技巧不好),但只有 E 段明确把“不会唱” 当作根源问题。

items.en: details of the physical processes involved when a person sings
items.zh: 描述人唱歌时身体内部的发声过程。
items.why: A 段从声带位置、呼吸时的状态，到说话 / 唱歌时气流推动声带振动、形成声音，一步步解释“身体里发生了什么”,正是题干所说 details of the physical processes involved when a person sings,因此选 A。

items.en: a defence of the use of surgery to treat vocal injuries
items.zh: 为用外科手术治疗发声损伤作辩护。
items.why: 这里 Zeitels 和 Sataloff 都在强调手术的积极作用: 手术+教育可以延长歌手生涯，虽然不完美，但“是一个选项”。这就是对手术的 defence (辩护、支持),因此 17 题选 F。E 段反而是批评手术只是暂时方案，不符合“辩护”。

items.en: a description of the initial indications of vocal problems
items.zh: 描述嗓音开始出现问题时的征兆。
items.why: 歌手常最先发现声音发颤、音准忽高忽低，这是受损声带无法正常共鸣的早期迹象。

items.en: a reference to modern perceptions of a good singing performance
items.zh: 提及现代对好歌唱表演的看法
items.why: 现代各类音乐表演中普遍有“越响越好”的看法，说明人们怎样评价好的歌唱表演。

items.en: The ________ of a sound is determined by the rate of vibration of the vocal cords.
items.zh: 声音的________由声带振动的频率决定。
items.why: 题干关键词 rate of vibration 对应原文 The greater the vibration,后半句给出结果 the higher the pitch,说明“振动频率决定音高”,因此空格应填 pitch。语法上用名词，与句子结构吻合。

items.en: The delicate surface of the vocal cords can be worn down by ________ if they are continually overused.
items.zh: 如果声带长期使用过度，其娇嫩的表面可能会因________而磨损。
items.why: 题干 worn down 对应原文的 eroae (侵蚀、魔损),continua/ly overused 对应 prolonged' overuse。导致表面被侵蚀的原因是 friction,故答案填 friction。

items.en: Singers with vocal cord damage are often unable to produce a sound with the correct ________ at a certain point on the musical scale.
items.zh: 声带受损的歌手在唱到音阶上的某个音时，往往无法发出________正确的声音。
items.why: 回到对应内容“音阶上常会出现一个“空洞”，即歌手声带虽在振动，却发不出正确音调”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Opera singers are often given a variety of ________ to make sure they can complete their performances.
items.zh: 为了让歌剧演员能够完成演出，人们常给他们使用多种 ________。
items.why: 题干的 a variety of 对应原文 numerous other, 后面紧跟的名词是 drugs,前面还有 steroid injections 作为一种药物方式，整体指“各种药物”,因此答案为 drugs。

items.en: Opera and classical performers are at greater risk of injury if they perform ________ which place exceptional demands on their voices.
items.zh: 歌剧和古典音乐表演者如果出演对嗓音要求特别高的________，受伤风险就会增加。
items.why: 回到对应内容“此外，至少在歌剧和古典音乐中，演员还可能接下须唱出天然音域之外的角色，种种因素使声带极易受伤”，再按题干要求写出答案。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

items.en: Surgery provides performers with only a short-term solution to their problems.
items.zh: 外科手术只为表演者提供短期解决其问题的办法。

items.en: The public are now used to attending performances given by singers with vocal injuries.
items.zh: 如今观众已经习惯观看嗓音受损的歌手登台演出。

items.en: People are wrong to suggest that performers who undergo surgical procedures to repair their voices lack singing ability.
items.zh: 人们错误地认为，接受手术以修复声音的表演者缺乏唱歌能力。

items.en: Surgery works best when used in conjunction with re-training performers.
items.zh: 手术配合歌手重新接受发声训练，效果最佳。

items.en: New and innovative surgical techniques hold the key to repairing damaged vocal cords.
items.zh: 新的和创新性的外科手术技术是修复受损声带的钥匙。

pairs: 短期解决办法／暂时的补救办法
The public are now used to
New and innovative surgical techniques hold the key
pioneering surgery is the way forward
创新的手术是解决问题的方向
points: 这里 Zeitels 和 Sataloff 都在强调手术的积极作用: 手术+教育可以延长歌手生涯，虽然不完美，但“是一个选项”。这就是对手术的 defence (辩护、支持),因此 17 题选 F。E 段反而是批评手术只是暂时方案，不符合“辩护”。
题干关键词 rate of vibration 对应原文 The greater the vibration,后半句给出结果 the higher the pitch,说明“振动频率决定音高”,因此空格应填 pitch。语法上用名词，与句子结构吻合。
clauses: For a singer, the first sign of trouble is often the ‘wobble’: the voice fluctuates on and off key ….
连接词 because 引出“because the damaged cords have lost the ability to resonate properly”，说明主句的原因关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 because 把这一层关系补进去。
There is no precise data on the number of performers who have undergone surgical procedures, but it is estimated ….
“that thousands have been under the knife”补足 estimated 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 estimated 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
